body.purpose: Use locally served IBM Plex Sans for the application.

graph-card.purpose: Graph labels use IBM Plex Sans with a generic sans-serif fallback.

shadows.name: temporary-filter-panel
shadows.purpose: Only the temporary filter panel uses a shadow.

motion.name: loading-line
motion.purpose: Loading indicator; the load keyframes translate from -90% to 190%.

motion.name: refresh-indicator
motion.purpose: Refresh indicator; the spin keyframes rotate to 360deg.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Disable animation and use automatic scrolling when prefers-reduced-motion is reduce.

graph.overview: Explicit fit-all view; titles and labels remain visible.

rendering.htmlOverlay: Number/status, open/label quick actions, colored label markers, and a right output port.

graph.readableAnchor: Keep the anchor card and quick actions within the viewport, with a 40px margin.

cardControls.clippedActions: Hidden; removed from keyboard focus with tabIndex -1.
cardControls.markerLimit: Three colored label markers with text; additional labels use a +count indicator.

portDrop.blankCanvas: Open an explicit connected-card creation form.
portDrop.invalidTarget: Do not create on the source card, external references, or outside the canvas.
portDrop.tapOrKeyboard: Activate connection mode and offer Neue Karte as a creation alternative.

connectedCreation.default: Create a real Task child under a source Issue.
connectedCreation.alternative: Create a related or directed blocking Issue; unsupported child sources default to a related Issue.
connectedCreation.submit: Create only after explicit form submission.

interaction.quickLabels: Read the current ticket and send only version-checked label additions/removals.

mouseInput.interaction: Left-button card selection, movement and connections
mouseInput.touch: Native one-finger pan and pinch zoom

graphLegend.examples: A/B ticket cards with actual line, triangle, vee and diamond styles
graphLegend.keyboard: Enter opens; Escape closes and restores summary focus

narrative.northStar: A restrained, light workspace for continuous project work.
narrative.overview:
A restrained, light workspace for continuous project work. Use a forest-green action accent, neutral panels,
and native GitLab status colors. The graph is the working surface, not a decorative illustration.
keyCharacteristics: Desktop uses a filter/result sidebar and a flexible graph. The inspector adds a third column only when a ticket is open.

Graph nodes are 284 by 224 model pixels and always include titles and labels.
The default readable zoom is 0.85; the explicit overview fits all nodes without substituting compact labels.
Pack disconnected components so isolated tickets do not form a single root row.
HTML controls follow the graph camera: number/status at the top left, open/label actions at the top right, colored
label markers at the bottom, and a round output port centered on the right edge. The port stays at a stable physical
size while zooming. Hide actions below zoom 0.5 and when clipped; keep them out of keyboard focus then.
Drop on a card to choose its relationship; drop on blank canvas to create a connected card, defaulting to a Task.
The creation form and quick label dialog use the same native dialog, explicit-save, and draft-protection conventions.

Connection mode supports two-tap selection, drawing, and target search. Source and target receive the same restrained
green selection treatment. The native dialog explains direction and requires a separate checkbox before closing
a duplicate. Purple dotted arrows point from a duplicate to its original. Never report a write as successful before
the GitLab result is read back and verified.

On coarse-pointer devices, controls have a minimum 44-pixel target, inputs use at least 16-pixel text, and hover styles
do not persist after tapping. Keep browser page zoom available; reserve canvas gestures for graph pan and pinch.
For a mouse, reserve right-button dragging for camera panning and left-button input for card interaction and connections.
Keep native one-finger pan and pinch on touch input, including hybrid touch/mouse devices.
Apply safe-area padding and contain overscroll within each panel. Test real-device behavior separately from emulation.
dos: Keep the viewport stable when selecting a ticket or changing its text.

Emphasize the selected card, its direct visible neighbors, and incident edges. Dim unrelated cards and their HTML controls together. Preserve edge colors and directions. Restore normal contrast when selection is cleared.

Restore each view's saved browser arrangement, with a separate arrangement for each label theme. Filters and GitLab refresh preserve known card positions. Place only unseen cards; move known cards by dragging or the explicit layout action. Show storage failures and unreadable saved positions in a persistent notice.
Retain visible errors and unsaved text until the user resolves them.
donts: Do not imply that a label cluster is a GitLab parent-child structure.
Do not use color alone to express status or make canvas interaction the only navigation path.
